acip: DE'I PHYIR SEMS BSKYED PA 'DI NI LAS KYI SGRIB PA THAMS CAD RNAM PAR SBYONG BAR BYED DE, JI SKAD DU GSUNGS PA BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' DE GAL TE SNGA DRO LTUNG BA BYUNG NA NYI MA PHYED NA BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS MNGON DU BYED PA DE'I TSUL KHRIMS KYI PHUNG PO MTHA' MED PA NYID DU RIG PAR BYA'O DE BZHIN DU RIGS KYI BU BSKAL PA'I ME DANG MNYAM PA'I BYANG CHUB KYIS SEMS NI NYES PAR SPYOD PA THAMS CAD SREG PAR BYED DO ZHES RGYA CHER RO
wylie: de'i phyir sems bskyed pa 'di ni las kyi sgrib pa thams cad rnam par sbyong bar byed de, ji skad du gsungs pa byang chub sems dpa' de gal te snga dro ltung ba byung na nyi ma phyed na byang chub kyi sems mngon du byed pa de'i tshul khrims kyi phung po mtha' med pa nyid du rig par bya'o de bzhin du rigs kyi bu bskal pa'i me dang mnyam pa'i byang chub kyis sems ni nyes par spyod pa thams cad sreg par byed do zhes rgya cher ro
english: And so we can say that anyone who is able to develop this particular version of the wish is able to clean from themselves, completely, each and every obstacle caused by their past bad deeds. This is the point of the scripture that states: Suppose any particular bodhisattva commits a transgression of their vows in the morning, but by noon has had a true feeling of the Wish for enlightenment. You should understand that they have created nothing but immeasurable mountains of pure conduct by spending their day this way. Again and again too we see statements then like "This Wish for enlightenment, o child of noble family, is equal in its strength to the fire that ends the world; it annihilates each and every bad deed you've ever done."
